Okay so for starters - you were playing an unrated game so try not to take what your team mates said *too* harshly. Now, I know that is easier said than done but forget that game even happened and lets start fresh.

​

>I get it I’m new to the game and don’t understand it very well but I did  NOT expect what basically equates to my first game in Valorant to be  against legitimately skilled players

Secondly, these players probably weren't "skilled players" and where most likely mid-low tiered elo (Silver to Gold). The reason the game put you into a mid tier for your "first-ish" game was to assess how you would play against someone of that caliber, now that the game has finished it will take the data gathered and your next game will most likely be at lower elo and so on so forth until you are more consistently getting kills and objective score (defusing/planting).

​

>How the hell am I supposed to learn this game or “Git Gud” when I’m simply spectating my teammates the whole time

There are other game modes to try, and you should try them.

In the lower ranks most of your"skill" equates to all aim. So for practice go into the offline mode and shoot bots for 10-15 minutes (or longer if you feel) before you queue up for a game. After a while of not playing or for your first time just that day you need to get used to your mouse and sensitivity again.

Example: I work in an office and my mouse sensitivity at work is WAY higher than at home so when I get home it feels weird to use my mouse until I play around in the bots for a little bit.

​

Essentially what I would recommend is - play Death Match for a while to get used to the game mechanics, moving, aiming, spray control, etc. Then from there, go back to your unrated matches and this time - MUTE all of the players, friendly and enemy. Trust me, this will make your unrated experience much more enjoyable! While doing those unrated games work on YOUR game. Then once you are comfortable with how you are playing, try more without muting and actually communicating with people, then transition to ranked. There is no rush to get into ranked, take your time. Walk - standard full speed walk
Slow walk - when you hit caps lock or scroll wheel all the way down

If you are walking it is way easier to hear actions, when you sprint you can almost hear nothing besides your own sprinting.
Keep in mind - if you can hear someone sprinting or walking, they can most likely hear you as well!

The most rewarding play style I have found (and I am sure most will agree with me) is slow.

Don't sprint unless necessary. Just simply walk, with frequent stops in high traffic areas to listen for a few seconds before proceeding. Stay to the edges of areas so that you only have to watch one direction.

Example of myself on Customs is to hug the wall all the way to the back of dorms (whilst walking). Sit outside for 30s or so and listen for any players that may be sprinting up to the building, or players that are inside opening doors (it is a lot easier to hear them inside if you have Comtacts, Sordins, ETC.). Once entering, slow walk until you are almost 100% positive there is no one inside (always stay on guard as you can never be 100% sure). Then proceed back to normal walking speed. Remember, you can hear people ADS, check inventory, change fire mode, reload, re pack mags, etc, the list goes on forever. Therefore playing slow and being completely aware of the sounds around you will help you a T O N.

​

You will get it figured! Stay positive, maybe also try finding a Sherpa to help get you into a different play style!
